rapport_notes: Professional and patient through a complex, detailed logistics conversation, but little warmth or personality; mostly transactional.
process_discipline_notes: Damage coverage and Meet Your Mover both mentioned in Stage 1 as direct answers to customer concerns AND mentioned again in Stage 2 (the big pitch block where all differentiators are listed together). No silence held after the agenda question or the estimate explanation—rep pivged immediately.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep does not frame the call with a time-boxed ask and promise of an accurate quote in return. Jumps straight into data collection.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'Do you have any special instructions, concerns or stressors about moving in general that you want me to take note of at this time.' Asked after ~20 minutes of logistics probing (pickup address, storage size, contents, distances, destination, etc.).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concern about cost (move is more expensive than expected). Joanna: 'I understand. Yup... of course, how organize it will be on the storage especially as you mentioned there are items that you can also move some of yourself. And definitely that's those factors can help make things quicker.' Also customer raised concern about mirror installation; Joanna explored that ('We actually do not...') and the customer worked through her own solution. On the cost surprise, Joanna acknowledged and offered email review as a follow-up mechanism.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Stage 1 direct answer: 'Joanna: ...do you think we have around 5060 boxes in that storage as well?' and 'anything oversized like a piano workout equipment, or a safe.' Customer named fragile/heavy items (solid oak furniture, mirror, recliner); Joanna acknowledged these. Stage 2 repeat: 'We also include other features like our no worries, damage coverage which would give you up to Tuesday $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Stage 1 direct answer: Customer asked 'can you remember how many trucks move you guys into the storage?' Joanna discussed crew size recommendation (three men). Stage 2 repeat: 'also meet your mover feature. Rest assured we don't take bily contract. The workers, our guys are the most we dead and movers in the industry and we'll send you their names ahead of time to let you know who's coming to help out with the move.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Stage 2 only: 'and lastly on time guarantee if we run late on the time, we schedule, we provide discounts by the end of the day.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Not mentioned anywhere in the call. No day-before call, no named crew lead, no inbox updates discussed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically a ten by twenty internal storage usually takes seven and a half to nine and a half with two men. Now in your case, including the travel time in between. So, we're already looking at about ten and a half hours...' Then: 'So, that would be eight to nine hour. So, which is an estimated budget of $2,810 including the travel fee already.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_window: Joanna: 'But of course, if it takes shorter than that, that's totally fine. You only pay for how long it will take after the twenty half hour minimum. So, the shorter it will be, the lower the cost.' (Repeated several times.)
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Joanna: 'You only pay for how long it will take after the twenty half hour minimum. So, the shorter it will be, the lower the cost.' and 'of course, the shorter it will be on the day, the lower the cost.'
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock line mentioned. No explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?'). Call ends with Joanna sending email: 'Okay, yeah, I'm sorry, I can't hear anything on the other line anymore but yeah, I'll go ahead and send everything in the email. Thank you so much and have a good day.'

top_strength: Joanna dug genuinely deep into the move logistics and customer concerns—she asked follow-up questions about distances, furniture details, and storage organization, and when the customer expressed cost shock, she articulated the factors driving the estimate and offered a sensible path forward (email review, possibility of photos).
coaching_note: Critical gaps: never frame the quid pro quo (time-boxed ask + quote promise), ask the agenda question *before* probing (not after 20 minutes), avoid saying a differentiator twice (damage coverage and Meet Your Mover both landed in Stage 1 AND Stage 2), mention Communication as part of the takeaway, and always end with an explicit close ask—you walked away without a clear next step or rate-lock confirmation.
